key_insight: Embedding random Fourier features into a PINN reduces spectral bias, allowing better recovery of sharp elastic-plastic gradients and failure zones in non-associative Mohr-Coulomb geomaterials.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster mesh-free surrogate for geotechnical elasto-plastic analysis, potentially reducing reliance on costly incremental FEM solves.
method: Random Fourier feature mapping added to the PINN input layer
Multi-objective loss enforces equilibrium, constitutive laws, and KKT conditions
Strain-adaptive sampling improves resolution near plastic zones
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark cases, FF-PINN outperformed a conventional PINN, cutting displacement error by up to about 66%, stress error by about 27%, and training time by roughly half while better matching FEM plastic-zone geometry.
watch_item: Performance is validated against FEM benchmarks, so real-world deployment still depends on careful tuning of loss weights, sampling strategy, and robustness to changing soil parameters or boundary conditions.
paper_title: Fourier Feature Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Elasto-Plastic Analysis of Geomaterials with a Non-Associative Mohr-Coulomb Model
